edges.mechanism: SOC is both habitat and energy source for bacteria, fungi and soil fauna; below ~0.5–1% the food web collapses toward oligotrophic specialists.
sources: FAO 2017 Soil Organic Carbon: the hidden potential
Barrios 2007 Ecological functions of soil fauna

edges.mechanism: Diverse microbial guilds mineralize N and P, form mycorrhizae, and stabilize aggregates that protect remaining carbon.
sources: Wagg et al. 2014 PNAS soil biodiversity and ecosystem multifunctionality

edges.mechanism: More even nutrient supply and symbiotic associations allow subordinate native plants to persist instead of a few nitrophilous weeds.
sources: van der Heijden et al. 2008 Ecology Letters mycorrhizal fungi

edges.mechanism: Structurally mixed plant canopies create niches for insects, birds and small mammals.
sources: Cardinale et al. 2012 Nature biodiversity loss

edges.mechanism: Heterogeneous habitats support more trophic levels and reduce competitive exclusion.
sources: Tews et al. 2004 Journal of Biogeography habitat heterogeneity

edges.mechanism: Precipitation is the primary input to plant-available water; in semi-arid systems small changes in infiltration dominate outcomes.
sources: Noy-Meir 1973 Annual Review of Ecology and Systematics

edges.mechanism: Humus and fungal hyphae increase aggregate stability and porosity, raising infiltration and plant-available water.
sources: Hudson 1994 Journal of Soil and Water Conservation

edges.mechanism: Higher infiltration stores rainfall in the root zone instead of losing it to runoff and evaporation.
Plant-available water is a first-order constraint on primary production and therefore on consumer diversity, especially in drylands.
sources: Maestre et al. 2012 Science dryland biodiversity

edges.mechanism: Small, isolated patches lose area-sensitive species, disrupt dispersal, and suffer edge-driven microclimate drying.
sources: Haddad et al. 2015 Science habitat fragmentation

edges.mechanism: Canopy loss raises surface temperature, vapor-pressure deficit and erosion, accelerating SOC oxidation.
sources: Lawrence and Vandecar 2015 Nature Climate Change

edges.mechanism: Forest conversion both reduces habitat area and increases isolation of remaining patches.
Insecticides (notably neonics) and some fungicides reduce wild bee survival, navigation and nesting success.
Animal pollination maintains sexually reproducing wild plants and many fruit/seed crops.
Community composition shifts strongly with pH; extreme acidity or alkalinity reduces functional guild richness.
sources: Fierer and Jackson 2006 PNAS soil bacteria pH

edges.mechanism: Topsoil holds most SOC and seeds; sheet erosion permanently exports the biologically active layer.
Heat and drought extremes disproportionately kill specialized and less-mobile species; diverse systems are more resistant.
Floral continuity and nesting substrates in hedgerows, fallows and forest edges sustain wild pollinators.
